describes: A Node web app with npm scripts: unit tests and a build on every change, Playwright e2e, a landing that waits for the production deployment GitHub reports for the merge, a scenarios harness that starts the dev server, and a policy draft.

recipes.name: unit tests
recipes.note: npm test; point it at your runner (vitest, jest, node --test) in package.json

recipes.name: the build
recipes.note: npm run build, so a type error or a broken import fails the check

recipes.name: Playwright end to end
recipes.note: npx playwright test; playwright.config webServer starts the app, as the scenarios harness does

land.name: the merge, deployed to production and live

steps.wait: s=$(gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/deployments?sha=$MERGE_SHA&environment=production&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].statuses_url // empty' 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$s" ] && gh api "$s" --jq '[.[] | select(.state=="success")][0].environment_url // empty' 2>/dev/null
steps.note: prints nothing until a production deployment of the merge reports success; stderr is discarded so an auth error is never read as a URL
prints the merge commit once the service says it runs it; replace with however yours reports its commit

scenarios.style: Write each scenario as a visit or a request against $BASE_URL: the page or endpoint, what a person does there, and what they see. Prefer what a user notices (a page, a form, a response code and body) over internals.
